learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the ultimate game of electron trading! Learn to track electrons using oxidation numbers, balance complex equations, and see how batteries generate power.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Classically, oxidation is adding oxygen/losing hydrogen. Modernly, Oxidation Is Loss of electrons (OIL), and Reduction Is Gain of electrons (RIG). They always happen together; you can't have one without the other!

A bookkeeping system for electrons! It is the imaginary charge an atom would have if all bonds were completely ionic. Free elements (like $O_2$ or $Na$) always have an oxidation number of $0$. Fluorine is always $-1$.
The substance that gets oxidized forces the other to be reduced, so it is the 'Reducing Agent'. The substance that gets reduced forces the other to be oxidized, so it is the 'Oxidizing Agent'.
A special type of redox reaction where the exact SAME element in a single reactant is simultaneously oxidized AND reduced to form two different products.

Devices that convert chemical energy of spontaneous redox reactions into electrical energy (like AA batteries). Oxidation always occurs at the Anode, and Reduction always occurs at the Cathode (Remember: 'An Ox and Red Cat').

fun_activity.title: 🍎 The Apple Rust
fun_activity.instructions: Cut an apple in half and leave it on a table. It turns brown in 10 minutes. This is a real-life Redox reaction! The enzymes in the apple react with oxygen in the air (oxidation). If you squeeze lemon juice (Vitamin C, a reducing agent) on the other half, it won't turn brown!

exam_tips: 📌 Balancing redox equations (using either the Ion-Electron method or Oxidation Number method) in both acidic and basic mediums is a guaranteed 3 or 5-mark question. Practice the steps rigorously!
📌 Identify the Oxidizing Agent / Reducing Agent carefully. The Oxidizing Agent is the one whose oxidation number decreases (it undergoes reduction).
📌 In calculating oxidation numbers, Oxygen is usually $-2$, except in peroxides (like $H_2O_2$) where it is $-1$, and superoxides where it is $-1/2$.
quick_recap: ⭐ The sum of all oxidation numbers in a neutral molecule is always zero. For a polyatomic ion, it equals the charge of the ion.
⭐ Anode is negative and Cathode is positive in a standard Galvanic cell.
⭐ A salt bridge is used in cells to maintain electrical neutrality and complete the circuit.
